thread:
Carla - Support: FYI customer "Acme Maps" on Dedicated pool is seeing p95/p99 spikes and 503s for the last ~30m. They reported affect on billing because retries are spiking. Escalating: they hit our SLA. :warning:
Ben - Oncall: Looking now. Do we have a link to the Grafana dashboard?
Carla - Support: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/8y7-inference/dedicated-pools?orgId=1&var-pool=acme-dedicated
Carla - Support: Key signals — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.4s, p99 at 5–7s. Error rate (5m) 2.7% 503s, 1.1% 429s.
infra-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-acme-sla-breach triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z
Ben - Oncall: I see a provisioning backlog on the pool. provisioner.log shows repeated "scale_up_backoff: waiting 30s" and queue depth grew to 18. Could be cold GPU start time.
Alice - SRE: Can you paste the provisioner logs? Also check driver init times — last time this happened a node's driver took ~3m to finish and k8s marked it NotReady.
Dinesh - Runtime: Pasting snippet from provisioner today:
```
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] provisioner: request_scale delta=6 -> desired=10 (min=1 max=20)
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] node-provision: launching g4dn-xlarge x6
[2026-03-15T08:47:30Z] node-provision: instance i-0abcd reached running
[2026-03-15T08:50:48Z] kubelet: kubelet lost connection to container runtime
[2026-03-15T08:52:40Z] node-provision: gpu-driver-install duration=190s
[2026-03-15T08:52:42Z] provisioner: scale_up_backoff waiting=30s attempt=3
[2026-03-15T08:53:10Z] provisioner: desired_active=6 ready_active=2 backlog=18
```
Dinesh - Runtime: So we have ~3 minute driver install / init window. That plus kubelet flaps explains p99s.
Maya - CS: Customer says they saw these spikes start during a regional load test at ~08:40 UTC — they abruptly ramped traffic. They expect us to protect them.
Alice - SRE: Root cause candidate = slow node bootstrap (driver/kernel module install) + conservative autoscaler cooldowns + min_replicas=1 for pool, so big capacity jumps needed causing long cold-start tail.
Ben - Oncall: Short mitigation suggestion: temporarily increase pool min_capacity from 1 -> 4 for acme-dedicated so existing warm GPUs available. Can we do that with config override?
Dinesh - Runtime: Yes we can change pool config. I'll push a short-lived override to set min_capacity=4 and bump warmup_target=2. Doing it now.
Dinesh - Runtime: `POST /admin/pools/acme-dedicated/config {"min_capacity":4,"warmup_target":2}` -> 202 Accepted.
infra-bot: config-change: acme-dedicated min_capacity 1 -> 4 by dinesh (runtime) at 2026-03-15T09:20:05Z
Ben - Oncall: After override p95 dropped to ~180ms within ~4m, p99 to ~600ms. Error rate down to 0.2% 503s. :thumbsup:
Carla - Support: I informed the customer about temporary change and apology. They asked for root cause analysis and permanent fix.
Alice - SRE: Permanent mitigations we should consider — (1) increase default min_capacity for Dedicated pools under bursty traffic profiles, (2) pre-warm logic to pre-install drivers earlier (image with driver baked in), (3) tune provisioner to parallelize driver install and container pull, (4) reduce aggressive scale_down to avoid having min=1 for production customers.
Dinesh - Runtime: Quick repro steps for devs:
1) Spin a pool with `min_capacity:1` and `max_capacity:20`
2) Run a ramp test with `wrk -t8 -c200 -d2m --script=seq_request.lua` where seq_request sends 100 concurrent model requests with seq_len=1024.
3) Observe provisioner logs and p99 tail in Grafana.
Suggested test script attached here: https://git.internal/redwood/qa/loadtests/acme-coldstart.lua
Alice - SRE: Also noticed the provisioner had a global rate limiter due to cloud account quota (we throttle new instances to 5/min). That makes it worse during large ramps. Need a rate-limiter bypass for SLA-backed Dedicated pools.
George - AM: Customer on an annual Dedicated contract — they expect SLA workarounds. Please include me in any customer comms.
Dinesh - Runtime: Proposed immediate action items:
- Keep temporary min_capacity=4 for 48h and monitor.
- Create a follow-up ticket to bake GPU drivers in base AMI to eliminate 180–200s install window.
- Add a provisioner bypass/priority path for Dedicated SLA pools.
- Add a warmup job that issues light inference calls after node ready to populate caches.
- Update runbook and add an autoscale playbook for rapid min_capacity adjustments.
Alice - SRE: I'll open SRE ticket and schedule a postmortem. Priority P1. Assign to runtime + infra. Include exact graphs and timestamps.
Carla - Support: Customer accepted temp fix, asked for ETA on permanent. Told them we'll follow up in 24h.
Ben - Oncall: Leaving notes in incident manager and adding PagerDuty summary.
infra-bot: incident-created: inc-2026-0415-41 (Assigned: runtime, sRE)
Dinesh - Runtime: One extra note — we saw an unusual number of cold-model loads (large model variant) during the ramp; recommend routing heavy models through dedicated warm subpool or use quantized variants for initial requests.
Alice - SRE: For the postmortem include: timeline, customer impact, provisioner logs, cloud account quota metrics, AMI build logs, recommendations and follow-up owners.
Maya - CS: I'll coordinate customer communication and provide them the postmortem draft.
Carla - Support: Thanks all — I'll monitor and close out after 24h stability window. :pray:
Ben - Oncall: If p99 climbs again, revert to emergency fallback: route traffic to hosted fallback model instance (non-dedicated) until Dedicated pool warmed. Documented in runbook.
Dinesh - Runtime: Adding follow-up tasks to backlog and will link PRs for AMI bake and provisioner priority.
Alice - SRE: Great work. Closing this thread; we'll follow with the postmortem ticket.
George - AM: Thanks team — appreciate quick response.
